name: Philip Dormer Stanhope, Earl of Chesterfield
credit: Portrait of the 4th Earl of Chesterfield by Allan Ramsay, 1765 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Philip Dormer Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield (1694–1773), was a statesman, diplomat and celebrated wit, now best known for his Letters to his Son on manners and the conduct of life.
The epigram here is the one James Parton printed under his name in his anthology of English humorous poetry.

poems.title: On a Full-length Portrait of Beau Marsh
poems.author: Philip Dormer Stanhope, Earl of Chesterfield
poems.collection: The Humorous Poetry of the English Language (ed. James Parton)
poems.text:
"Immortal Newton never spoke
More truth than here you'll find;
Nor Pope himself e'er penn'd a joke
More cruel on mankind.

"The picture placed the busts between,
Gives satire all its strength;
Wisdom and Wit are little seen--
But Folly at full length."
